### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a4547a6a521e68fcbf7df1917983775aac12618` — the merge of head `483e6f51f3cc515a387e4c9d6e50f9c3a4e7e6e5` into base `28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a4547a6a521e68fcbf7df1917983775aac12618 && git checkout 6a4547a6a521e68fcbf7df1917983775aac12618
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e 483e6f51f3cc515a387e4c9d6e50f9c3a4e7e6e5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e && git merge --no-ff 483e6f51f3cc515a387e4c9d6e50f9c3a4e7e6e5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.field-group-related-list-side-card-refused.ts`**, against `isGroupPlaceableRelationship` / `fieldGroupBodyTableRefusal` on `main`:

- `surface`: the refused set is now "a lookup or master_detail FK declaring relatedList true or false, a lookup with no relatedList, or a bare child name one of whose FKs is any of those". The predicate returns false exactly for: a non-`'primary'` declared value on either type (true, false), and an absent value on a `lookup`; the refusal fires for a bare name when ANY named FK is unplaceable. The enumeration is complete and exact; the removed shape (plain `master_detail`, no `inlineEdit`) is accepted by the predicate. Holds.
- `replacement`: "`relatedList: 'primary'`, or for a master_detail remove an explicit `relatedList: true`". Removing `true` leaves an absent value on a `master_detail`, which the predicate accepts and the naming group then makes a body table (`isBodyTableRelationship` with `placedByGroup`). The `field.zod.ts` describe says the same from the other side ("Write true on a master_detail field to keep it an auxiliary panel even from a field group"). Dropping "inline-edited" is right: `inlineEdit` takes no part in the verdict. Holds.
- `reason` parenthetical: word for word the predicate in the refusal sentence ("a FK declaring relatedList: 'primary', or a master_detail FK that declares no relatedList, which the group makes one"). Holds.
- `reason`, "Ruling B keeps the FK's declared relatedList authoritative": true as far as it goes (a declared `true` / `false` cannot be overridden by a group; module header: "which a group cannot override"). See N1.
- The untouched stored-row paragraph ("an inline-edited master_detail FK declaring relatedList true was drawn as a body table, and is a side card now") is still true under the merged predicate.
- Break attempt, a stored group naming a plain `master_detail`: before the widening it drew nothing and its next save was refused; now it is accepted and drawn. The entry no longer claims it is refused, and `acceptanceCriteria` ("A group naming a body table ... parse and publish byte-identically") stays true. No contradiction found.
- Header comment: names `isGroupPlaceableRelationship` and "since #35597 ... whatever its inlineEdit"; the module header on `main` says "The set a group may name is the set #35597 accepted, unchanged". Agrees.

**`18.page-slots-tabs-retired.ts`**, against `PAGE_SLOTS_TABS_REMEDY` and the `kind` describe on `main`:

- `replacement` tail: "drawn as authored on the desktop full record page (a phone and the side preview draw the standard record page, with the composed strip)" is verbatim the remedy at `page.zod.ts:1229-1231`, and agrees with the `kind` describe (`page.zod.ts:2165`). Holds.
- `acceptanceCriteria`: "either the synthesized strip ... or, for a `kind: 'full'` page on the desktop full record page, the same tabs it showed before". On a phone or in the side preview a `kind: 'full'` page falls to the first arm (the standard page's composed strip), so the either/or is exhaustive and true. Holds.
- Break attempt, the platform's own approval-request and user pages (which the `reason` names as moved to `kind: 'full'`) keep their page on every surface per the `kind` describe; the entry's parenthetical states the general rule without that exception. It is the same sentence the live remedy prints, so the entry and the code cannot be read apart. Not a finding.

**`page-slots-tabs-retirement.test.ts`** (implementing: the entry's pin): the only change is one docblock line, now matching `page.zod.ts:2185-2186`. No assertion changed; the pin's three assertions hold on the new text (①).

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit): `reason` says ruling B "keeps the FK's declared relatedList authoritative". A `lookup` that declares no `relatedList` is also refused, and there it is the FK's type, not a declared value, that decides. The preceding clause ("the FK's own keys") covers it, so nothing false is taught. Accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit): the entry still calls a non-body list "a side card in the related column" (`reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`), where the page now draws a tab plus a rail card. Pre-existing, outside card 35701's ask, and the refusal sentence on `main` itself still says "a side card", so the entry agrees with the message the author sees. Follow-up card at the seat's discretion, together with the refusal sentence.
